_readme.what: How-To Guides — first-hand procedural knowledge for the tenant library's How-To section.
_readme.who: Entries are written from Brad's first-hand experience. Each guide is a real procedure that has actually been done, not theory.
_readme.how_to_add_an_entry: Copy the '_entry_template' object into 'guides', give it a new id, fill the fields, set status to 'published' when ready. Entries with any other status are hidden from the app.

fields.title: plain-language title — what the person is trying to do
fields.summary: one or two sentences — what this guide gets them
fields.steps: ordered list; each step has a short 'title' and a 'body' explaining what to actually do
fields.images: optional list of screenshots shown after the steps; each has 'src' (a /static/... path, e.g. /static/img/howto/my-guide-1.png), 'alt' (what the image shows — required), and optional 'caption'
fields.tips: optional list of things learned the hard way — what to watch for
fields.related_subjects: library subjects this guide relates to (see taxonomy.py ALL_SUBJECTS)
fields.source: 'first_hand' for Brad's experience; anything else needs a note
fields.status: 'placeholder' = skeleton only, hidden | 'draft' = written, hidden | 'published' = shown

guides.title: How to build pressure the right way: complaints, city leaders, and press — in order
guides.summary: The accountability sequence that actually moves a landlord: document first, get advice, file real complaints, put city leaders on notice, then go public. Each step feeds the next.

steps.title: Document everything before you say anything
steps.body: Every step after this one leans on dated, verifiable records — the notice, the repair request, the inspection report. Timeline, journal, and your document vault are the foundation; pressure built on memory gets waved off.

steps.title: Get advice before filing
steps.body: Talk to legal aid or a tenant hotline first. They'll tell you which complaints fit your facts, which deadlines apply, and whether your situation has a presumption window open right now.

steps.title: File the real complaints
steps.body: File with the agencies that actually have jurisdiction — attorney general, housing/code enforcement, HUD if discrimination is in play, the licensing board if the landlord or broker is licensed. Each filing creates an official record and an investigation the landlord has to answer to.

steps.title: Put city leaders on notice
steps.body: Send a factual letter to your council member, the mayor, or your county commissioner. Not a rant — what you documented, who you filed with, and what you're asking their office to do. City leaders can route inspections and put the landlord on notice that a record exists.

steps.title: Go public only when the record can carry it
steps.body: A press release or media kit works when the facts speak for themselves. Stick to what you can document — a truthful press release is pressure a landlord can't make go away; an exaggerated one gets set aside.

steps.title: Follow up on a schedule
steps.body: Agencies and offices respond to documented persistence. Log every contact, note every deadline they give you, and follow up when it passes. The record of follow-ups itself becomes part of the pressure.

tips: Filing with multiple agencies at once is legitimate — each has different leverage.
Everything you send to a leader or reporter should be something you'd be comfortable seeing in a courtroom. Facts only.
This is accountability, not revenge — the record does the talking. If a step would only embarrass someone rather than create a record or an obligation, skip it.
guides.source: research — system procedure, not first-hand experience; review before publishing

guides.title: Mark the bill draft: comment, question, or suggest an edit
guides.summary: How to leave a comment, ask a question, or suggest an edit on the Rent Assurance & Deposit Protection Act draft at semptify.org/bill. What you send stays private until a person reads it onto the public margin.

steps.title: Open the Inkwell
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open the page called the Inkwell. If you are reading a specific clause, use the mark link on that clause's page — it opens the same form with the clause already picked.

steps.title: Pick the clause and the kind
steps.body: Choose the clause your mark is about, or leave it on general, no clause. Then pick a kind: Comment, Question, or Proposed edit.

steps.title: Write it plainly
steps.body: Say what you mean in your own words — a suggestion, a concern, a correction, or a question all count. The writing box is required. Everything else on the form is optional.

steps.title: Decide what to sign
steps.body: You can add proposed wording, your name, and a way to reach you. Your name appears publicly only if a steward reads your mark onto the margin. Your contact information is never shown.

steps.title: Send it and save the receipt code
steps.body: Submit the form. The page gives you a receipt code — write it down. It is the only way to check on your mark later.

tips: Nothing posts right away. Your mark goes into a private intake pile. A person — called a steward — reads it and decides whether it goes on the public margin with an M-number.
Leave the name field blank to stay unsigned. The contact field is never published — it is only so the steward can reach you.
The box labeled website is a trap for bots. Leave it empty.
If this is about your own housing right now — a notice, a repair, a lockout — call HOME Line at 612-728-5767 first. The mark form says so too. A proposed law cannot fix an emergency.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-22; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Answer a mark that is already on the margin
guides.summary: How to reply to a mark someone already made on the bill draft at semptify.org/bill. Your answer links back to their mark once it is read in.

steps.title: Open the margin
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open the margin. It is the public ledger of every mark that has been read in — numbered M-0001 and up.

steps.title: Find the mark you want to answer
steps.body: Read down the list, or follow a link to a specific M-number. Each mark shows its number, its date, and the clause it is about.

steps.title: Choose 'answer by reference'
steps.body: On the mark, click or tap 'answer by reference.' It opens the Inkwell form already linked to that mark.

steps.title: Write your answer
steps.body: Say what you would add, correct, or answer. Keep it on the point you are replying to.

steps.title: Send it and save the receipt code
steps.body: Submit, then write down the receipt code. Once a steward reads your answer in, it shows on the margin as a reply to that M-number.

tips: Answers are marks too — they go through the same private intake before they show publicly.
Answer the mark, not the person. The margin is a public record, and plain and factual reads best.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-22; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Ask for a briefing, an amendment, a position, or an answer
guides.summary: How to use the requests desk at semptify.org/bill when you need more than a comment — a briefing, a change to the draft, an organization's position, or a technical answer. You can watch your request move through its stages.

steps.title: Open the requests desk
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Requests. The form for a new request is on that page.

steps.title: Pick what you are asking for
steps.body: Choose a request type: Briefing / fiscal walkthrough, Statutory amendment, Organization position, Technical question, or Other.

steps.title: Say it in one line
steps.body: The summary box is required — one line that says what you are asking. You can also pick the clause it relates to and add details underneath.

steps.title: Say who is asking — optional
steps.body: There is a field for your organization or role, and a contact field. The contact is for the steward only. It never shows on the public page.

steps.title: Send it and save the receipt code
steps.body: Submit the form and write down the receipt code. It is the only way to check on your request later.

tips: A request is for something that needs an answer or an action. If you only want to comment on the wording of a clause, use the Inkwell instead.
Your request moves through stages: new, reviewing, scheduled, then incorporated or declined. Check it anytime with your receipt code on the Track page.
Notes the steward leaves on your request are public. Read your request's row to see them.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-22; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Sign the bill
guides.summary: How to add your name to the public book of supporters for the Rent Assurance & Deposit Protection Act draft at semptify.org/bill. Signing is a public act — your name publishes only because you choose it.

steps.title: Open the sign page
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Sign the bill.

steps.title: Write your name as it should appear
steps.body: The name field is required. Whatever you write is what would publish — for example, A. Renter, St. Paul.

steps.title: Add what you want on the record — optional
steps.body: You can add your organization or town, and one line for the record. Both publish with your name.

steps.title: Add your email only if you want follow-up — optional
steps.body: The email field is never published. It exists so someone can reach you about the bill.

steps.title: Tick the consent box and send
steps.body: The 'Publish my name' checkbox is required — it is your clear yes. Submit the form, then save the receipt code.

tips: Signing lands dark first. Your name publishes only after a steward reads it in — then it gets an S-number in the public book.
The consent checkbox is what makes signing possible at all. No tick, no signature — the form will not send.
Name, org or town, and your line for the record are the only things that can appear. Email is never published.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-22; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Check on something you sent
guides.summary: How to use a receipt code to see where your mark, request, or signature stands on the bill platform at semptify.org/bill. The receipt code is the only way back — nothing public ties a submission to you.

steps.title: Find your receipt code
steps.body: Every time you submit a mark, request, or signature, the page shows a receipt code — a short string of letters and numbers — and tells you to save it. Look where you wrote it down.

steps.title: Open the track page
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Track a submission.

steps.title: Enter the code
steps.body: Type or paste the code into the Receipt code box and submit.

steps.title: Read the status
steps.body: The page shows where your submission stands. A mark shows queued or read in — once read in, it shows its M-number and a link to the margin. A signature shows queued or published with its S-number. A request shows its stage: new, reviewing, scheduled, incorporated, or declined.

tips: The receipt code is the only lookup. If you lose it, there is no way to find your submission — save it every time.
Your code is private to you. It never shows on the public pages, and the public pages never show who sent what.
Nothing appearing for a while is normal — a steward reads things in by hand. Check again later with the same code.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-22; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Read the draft your way
guides.summary: How to read the Rent Assurance & Deposit Protection Act draft at semptify.org/bill — through the lens that fits you, in legal wording or plain language, one clause or the whole record.

steps.title: Open the draft
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open The bill. The draft is 23 clauses across a preamble and four titles, laid out in order.

steps.title: Pick your lens
steps.body: Near the top, choose Renter lens, Provider lens, or Lawmaker lens. The notes under each clause change to speak to that reader.

steps.title: Choose how it reads
steps.body: The default shows the legal wording with an 'In plain language' reading under it. The 'Plain only' link hides the legal wording so you can read just the plain version.

steps.title: Open one clause
steps.body: Click a clause code, like I-2, for its own page — the wording, the audience notes, its sources, its margin, and a mark form for that clause.

steps.title: Search the whole record
steps.body: Open Search and type a word or phrase. One query covers the clauses, margin marks, changes, requests, editions, and locked decisions.

tips: The platform picks a screen layout for your device. You can change it yourself — Auto, Desktop, TV / Present, or Mobile / Tablet in the top bar.
This is a working draft, not filed law. The plain-language text is a reading aid, and the page says so.
Select any phrase in the draft and the toolbar offers to mark it or propose an edit — the fastest way from reading to speaking.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Read the margin: the public ledger
guides.summary: How to read the margin at semptify.org/bill — every mark that has been read in, numbered and dated, with the Drafting Table's answers inline.

steps.title: Open the margin
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open The margin. It is the public ledger — every mark a steward has read onto the record, numbered M-0001 and up.

steps.title: Read a mark
steps.body: Each mark shows its number, its date, its kind — comment, question, or proposed edit — the clause it is about, and who signed it.

steps.title: Read the answer
steps.body: Official answers sit right under the mark they answer. 'Drafting Table' answers the substance. 'Statutory Review Lane' logs a point for the legal wording.

steps.title: Follow the replies
steps.body: Answers to earlier marks show 're: M-0001' so you can follow the chain. The # on each mark is a link you can copy to point at that exact mark.

tips: Only read-in marks appear. A mark you sent stays private until a person reads it in — check its status with your receipt code on the Track page.
A retracted mark stays visible, struck through, with a note. The record does not erase; it amends in the open.
Marks made on an open change proposal show as 'a contributor' — names are collected but never displayed there.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Weigh in on a proposed wording change
guides.summary: How to join the discussion on an open change proposal at semptify.org/bill — the ledger where every proposed and incorporated change is decided in the open.

steps.title: Open Changes
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Changes. It is the ledger of every proposed, incorporated, declined, and retracted change.

steps.title: Find an open proposal
steps.body: Choose the Proposed filter to see what is still open. Each card shows the change, the clause it touches, and its close date. If nothing is open, the page says so.

steps.title: Read before you mark
steps.body: Read the proposal and the discussion marks already under it so you are adding to the conversation, not repeating it.

steps.title: Add a discussion mark
steps.body: On an open proposal, write your mark in its discussion. It is collected like any mark, but it displays as 'a contributor' — your name is never shown on a change discussion.

tips: Nothing is deleted, only resolved. When a steward resolves a proposal, a public reason note is required — the reason is part of the record.
Only steward names appear on resolutions, and only with their consent. The steward roster names who holds that authority.
A comment on wording that is not tied to a proposal belongs on the Inkwell instead — it can still be read onto the margin.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Record where an organization stands
guides.summary: How to put an organization, coalition, or office on the public positions ledger at semptify.org/bill — who stands where, on what, dated and sourced.

steps.title: Open Positions
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Positions — 'Who stands where.' The record form is on that page.

steps.title: Say who
steps.body: Fill in Who — an organization, coalition, or office. This is required, and it is what publishes.

steps.title: Pick a stance
steps.body: Choose one: Supports, Opposes, Conditional, Neutral, or Watching.

steps.title: Name the provision
steps.body: Say what the stance is about — a title, a clause, or the whole draft. This is required too.

steps.title: Add a public source and record it
steps.body: A source is optional — a letter, testimony, or a meeting date. Then press Record position. It goes straight onto the public ledger.

tips: Positions post publicly right away. Unlike marks, there is no private intake step — record only what should be public.
Everything shows on the ledger: who, the stance, the provision, the date, and the source.
This form is for organizations and offices. To speak as yourself, mark the draft or sign the bill instead.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Test the funding math with your own rent
guides.summary: How to use the funding braid calculator at semptify.org/bill — put in a rent and see what the three-source assurance pool would cost, including the stress scenarios.

steps.title: Open the Funding Braid calculator
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Funding Braid. It tests the draft's three-source funding math against the 2026-10-23 audit, tied to Clause II-3.

steps.title: Enter your numbers
steps.body: Fill in a monthly rent, the number of units, and whether the renter qualifies for the MN Renter's Credit — the M1PR credit, for incomes up to $77,570.

steps.title: Read the three legs
steps.body: Press Calculate. Leg 1 is escrowed deposit float. Leg 2 is the renter share, carried by the M1PR advance. Leg 3 is the landlord matched share. Together they make the assurance pool, shown as a percent of rent.

steps.title: Read the stress scenarios
steps.body: Below the result are three cases: the base case, a claims shock of plus 30 percent, and a recession shock of 6 percent statewide default. Each shows the cost per unit per month.

tips: Figures marked 'estimate' are derived openly and awaiting actuarial review — the platform says that itself, and the Claims ledger shows which figures are verified and which are estimates.
If the renter qualifies for M1PR, the renter share shows $0.00 a month in new out-of-pocket — it rides on a tax credit that already exists.
Try the rent you actually pay. The point of the calculator is to check the claim against your own numbers, not the platform's.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Send the draft to your legislator
guides.summary: How to email the bill draft to the people who represent you in St. Paul — the campaign page at semptify.org/bill opens your mail with the ask already written.

steps.title: Find who represents you
steps.body: Open the Minnesota Legislature's 'Who Represents Me' tool at gis.lcc.mn.gov/iMaps/districts and type your address. It gives you your House and Senate members and their contact information.

steps.title: Open the Campaign page
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Campaign. It tracks the push for the 2027 session — targets, contacted, in talks, endorsed — in the open.

steps.title: Choose 'Send the draft to your legislator'
steps.body: In the 'Do one thing' section, that link opens your mail app with the subject and the ask pre-written.

steps.title: Address it and send
steps.body: Paste in your legislator's address, add a line of your own if you want, and send. The written ask is short — read the draft, and carry it in the 2027 session.

tips: One specific note to your own representative gets read. A line about why housing matters to you, in your words, carries more than the form text alone.
The campaign page also shows the other small jobs — sign the bill, mark the draft, request a briefing, print the testimony packet. One is enough.
Nothing is uploaded or stored when you use the mail link — it just opens your own mail app.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Teach the bill or print the testimony packet
guides.summary: How to walk a room through the draft at semptify.org/bill — a 14-stop teaching path, an 8-slide TV deck, and a printable packet of every mark on the record.

steps.title: Open Teach
steps.body: Go to semptify.org/bill and open Teach. It is a guided path of 14 stops, plain language first, built for classrooms, tenant meetings, and kitchen-table briefings.

steps.title: Walk the stops in order
steps.body: Each stop names a clause, gives the plain-language reading, and ends with a 'Talk about' prompt — one question to discuss before moving on.

steps.title: Present the deck if you have a screen
steps.body: The TV briefing deck is 8 slides. Use the arrow keys or number keys to move, F for fullscreen, and Esc to return to the desk. Speaker notes are built in.

steps.title: Print the testimony packet
steps.body: Open Testimony packet to get every read-in mark grouped by clause. Print it or save it as a PDF — that is what goes in a committee folder.

tips: The 'Student view (plain)' link lets a class or a meeting follow along in plain language on their own screens.
The packet only holds marks already read onto the margin — it grows as the public record grows, so print it close to the day you need it.
Teach the path, present the deck, leave the packet. Each piece does one job, and they work in that order.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: If this is about your own housing right now
guides.summary: The bill platform is for shaping a proposed law — it cannot take a case or answer an emergency. Here is where to reach real help first.

steps.title: If it is urgent, call first
steps.body: For an emergency, call 911. For a mental health or suicide crisis, call or text 988 — it runs around the clock. You can also text HOME to 741741.

steps.title: For a housing problem, call HOME Line
steps.body: HOME Line is 612-728-5767 — legal help for Minnesota renters on deposits, evictions, repairs, and notices. This is the line the mark form itself points to.

steps.title: For referrals and legal aid
steps.body: Dial 2-1-1 for statewide referrals to shelter, rent help, utilities, and food. LawHelpMN.org is the statewide legal-aid directory.

steps.title: Then come back to the draft
steps.body: Once the immediate problem has a path, the platform is still here — your read on the draft and your marks still shape what it becomes.

tips: A proposed law cannot fix an emergency — that is why the mark form carries the crisis note. The help lines exist for the urgent part.
The Help page on the platform lists only official public channels. Nothing there is an advertisement, and nobody paid to be listed.
Phone numbers change. The service's own website is the authority — the platform's Help page is a pointer, not a directory of record.
guides.source: verified against the live bill platform (semptify.org/bill) on 2026-11-23; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Log a call, email, text, or visit
guides.summary: How to put a landlord contact on your record — the date, how it happened, who it was, and what was said — using the comms log in the Semptify app.

steps.title: Open the comms log
steps.body: In the app, open the comms log — it sits with your record pages, next to Timeline and Journal. Your storage needs to be connected; the page says so if it is not.

steps.title: Set the date and the method
steps.body: Pick the date it happened, then how it happened: phone call, email, text, in person, letter, or other.

steps.title: Say who it was
steps.body: Choose who was on the other end — landlord, property manager, maintenance, your attorney or advocate, or other.

steps.title: Write what was said
steps.body: In the notes box, put down what was actually said — especially any promises, deadlines, or warnings, in their words where you can.

steps.title: Log it
steps.body: Tick 'This is a record' when the contact matters — a promise, a refusal, a warning. Then press Log contact. It lands on your timeline as a communication entry, dated.

tips: Log it while it is fresh. Same-day notes carry the details you will want later.
The 'This is a record' box marks the entry as important on your timeline — use it for anything you may need to point back to.
Every logged contact shows in the list below the form, dated, so you can see the pattern building.
guides.source: verified against app/templates/pages/comms_log.html and the /api/timeline/events + /api/timeline/unified calls it makes on 2026-11-24; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Capture a conversation while it is fresh
guides.summary: How to use quick capture in the Semptify app to record something that just happened — a conversation, a phone call, a notice — with photos, files, or audio attached.

steps.title: Open quick capture
steps.body: From your home page, open quick capture. To start on a conversation specifically, the capture link for conversations opens it with the Conversation card already picked.

steps.title: Pick the kind of thing
steps.body: Tap the card that fits: Got a Notice, Conversation, Phone Call, Repair Issue, Feeling Pressured, Payment Issue, or Something Else. Phone Call opens extra boxes — which way the call went, who it was, and how long it lasted.

steps.title: Say what happened
steps.body: Describe it in your own words — what was said, what was done. That box is required. Add the date, and if you want, the time, who was involved, and where.

steps.title: Attach what you have
steps.body: Add photos, documents, or recordings — upload files, or capture a photo or audio right there. The page may ask to use your camera or microphone; allow it only if you are recording.

steps.title: Save it
steps.body: Press Save This Record. The entry lands on your record, dated, with anything you attached.

tips: You can speak instead of type — the microphone next to 'What happened' takes dictation.
'This is a priority' flags the entry for attention — save it for the ones that truly are.
Quick capture is built for the moment. For a routine call you are logging afterward, the comms log asks the same questions with less to fill in.
guides.source: verified against app/templates/pages/tenant_capture.html on 2026-11-24; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Open, sign, or decline a document sent to you
guides.summary: How to handle a document an advocate, attorney, or manager sends you in the Semptify app — read it in your inbox, then sign it, acknowledge it, or decline it with a reason.

steps.title: Open your office inbox
steps.body: In the app, open Office, then Inbox. Anything sent to you lands there — the unread count shows what is new.

steps.title: Open the delivery
steps.body: Tap the item. Opening it marks it as read for the record and shows the notice — what kind of action it asks for and who sent it.

steps.title: Read before you act
steps.body: Read the document and the note that came with it. If it has a deadline, the notice says so.

steps.title: Choose your action
steps.body: Sign Document signs it — a confirm step asks you to be sure first. Acknowledge says you saw it. Reject declines it — you can give a reason, and the sender is told. Save to Vault keeps a copy in your record.

steps.title: Check it landed
steps.body: After an action the page confirms it and the inbox refreshes. Signed and acknowledged items show their new state on your record.

tips: The inbox refreshes itself when something new arrives — the page may ask to allow notifications.
Declining is a real answer, not a failure — give the reason so the record shows why.
Only the send side is limited to professionals. Everything that lands in your inbox is yours to act on.
guides.source: verified against app/templates/pages/office_inbox.html and app/modules/document_delivery/router.py on 2026-11-24; drafted per handoffs/library-guide-outline.md

guides.title: Share your case with a reviewer
guides.summary: How to give an attorney, advocate, or legal-aid reviewer a private link to the parts of a case you choose — and how to answer the questions they leave you.

steps.title: Open Share your case file
steps.body: In the app, open Legal Share — the page is called 'Share your case file.' It walks you through one choice at a time, top to bottom.

steps.title: Pick the case and what to include
steps.body: Choose the case, then check what the reviewer can see. Filed documents and exhibits start checked; drafts stay unchecked. Decide whether to include your case notes and the case summary.

steps.title: Say who it is for
steps.body: Name the reviewer — for yourself, like 'Attorney Lee' or 'legal aid intake.' You can add their email or phone and a short note they see at the top of the page.

steps.title: Set how long the link works
steps.body: Choose 7, 30, or 90 days. When it expires — or when you turn it off — the link stops working.

steps.title: Create and send the link
steps.body: Press 'Create the link,' then copy it or use 'Send by email.' The reviewer opens it with no sign-in and reads only what you checked.

steps.title: Watch for questions
steps.body: Back on the same page, 'Questions from reviewers' shows anything they asked, with the share it belongs to. Write your answer there — it goes back on the same thread.

tips: Treat the link like handing someone the paper — anyone who has it can read what you checked, including people it gets forwarded to.
If a lawyer sent you a document first, ask them before sharing it on — passing it along can undo the confidentiality that protects lawyer-client work.
Documents open exactly as they sit in your record, including details saved inside the file. Check anything sensitive before you share.
You can turn a link off anytime from 'Your shared links.' Nothing is sent automatically — you choose who gets it.

guides.title: Get an answer back to a professional
guides.summary: The Semptify app has no open chat page. Reaching a professional back works through two doors — answering a reviewer's questions on a shared case, or responding to a document they delivered to you.

steps.title: If a reviewer asked a question
steps.body: Open Legal Share — 'Share your case file.' 'Questions from reviewers' shows each question and the share it belongs to. Write your answer there; it goes back on the same thread.

steps.title: If a document needs a response
steps.body: Open Office, then Inbox, and open the delivery. Acknowledge says you saw it. Reject lets you decline and give a reason — the reason goes back to the sender.

steps.title: If you need to start the conversation
steps.body: Create a share link so they can read the case and ask you questions inside it — or reach them the way you normally do. Semptify does not send open messages for you yet.

tips: Unread questions are counted on your shared links — check back after you send one.
Replies on a share stay attached to that share, so both sides see the same context.
A reason on a declined delivery is part of the record — plain and factual reads best.
